v.q: What is the relationship between OpenShift and Kubernetes?
o: OpenShift is a Kubernetes distribution with added security, builds, routes and Operators
OpenShift is an alternative orchestrator that replaces Kubernetes completely
Kubernetes is a plugin that runs inside an OpenShift cluster
They are the same product sold under two names by different vendors
v.w: OpenShift contains standard Kubernetes, so Deployments, Services and ConfigMaps work unchanged. It adds platform features on top.

v.q: Which statement about OpenShift is NOT true?
v.w: OpenShift is a Kubernetes distribution with extra features, so kubectl concepts still apply.

v.q: An image that runs fine on Docker fails on OpenShift with permission errors. What is the most likely cause?
o: The default SCC runs it as a random non-root user, but the image expects root
OpenShift cannot pull images that were built on Docker
The router blocks all containers that expose port 8080
The image is too large for the integrated registry
v.w: The restricted-v2 Security Context Constraint forces a random non-root UID (group 0). Fix the image rather than granting anyuid.

v.q: Which Security Context Constraint behaviour surprises image authors?
o: Containers run as a random non-root user
Containers run as root by default
v.w: The restricted SCC assigns a random UID, so an image that needs root fails.

v.q: In an OpenShift pod, files the application must write should be owned or writable by which group?
o: Group 0, because the random UID is always in the root group
The group named after the project
Group 1001, which every image must create at build time
No group, because OpenShift disables file permissions
v.w: Use chgrp -R 0 and chmod -R g=u so the random user can write through its root group membership.

v.q: Which group should own a directory that a random user must write to?
v.w: The random UID always belongs to the root group, so group-writable files work.

v.q: What does an OpenShift Route do?
o: Publishes a Service on a hostname through the router, with TLS options and weights
Defines which node a pod is scheduled on, using labels and taints on the workers
Restricts which images may be pulled from the integrated registry by a project
Creates a Git webhook that starts a new build whenever a commit is pushed
v.w: A Route is OpenShift's way to expose a Service externally. Ingress objects also work and are translated into Routes.

v.q: Which resource exposes a Service on a hostname through the OpenShift router?
v.w: A Route is the OpenShift way. It supports TLS modes and traffic weights.

v.q: Which Route TLS termination encrypts traffic on both the client leg and the leg to the pod while letting the router inspect requests?
o: None, routes cannot use TLS to the pod
v.w: Edge ends TLS at the router, passthrough ends it at the pod without inspection, and re-encrypt does both legs with the router in the middle.

v.q: Which Route TLS mode lets the router terminate TLS and send plain HTTP to the pod?
v.w: Edge decrypts at the router. Re-encrypt creates a new TLS connection to the pod. Passthrough does not decrypt.

o: A build strategy that injects source into a builder image to create an image
A tool that converts a running container back into the source code it was built from
A network protocol for copying image layers between two registries in different clusters
A way of mounting a Git repository directly into a running pod as a writable volume
v.w: S2I combines your code with a builder image (for example Java) and commits a runnable image. A BuildConfig describes it.

v.q: Which build strategy needs no Dockerfile?
v.w: S2I combines your source with a builder image to produce the application image.

v.q: What is an Operator in Kubernetes and OpenShift?
o: A controller that manages an application through a custom resource
A human administrator role that holds cluster-admin rights over every project
A command line plugin for oc that formats the output of get commands as tables
A type of node that runs only infrastructure pods such as the router and registry
v.w: You declare desired state in a custom resource; the Operator reconciles the application to match. OLM installs and updates Operators.

v.q: Which statement about Operators is NOT true?
v.w: An Operator is software that encodes operational knowledge, not a person.

v.q: Which approach is recommended for new applications instead of the deprecated DeploymentConfig?
o: A bare Pod with a restart policy of Always
A StatefulSet for every stateless service
A Route with a replica count
v.w: DeploymentConfig is deprecated; Deployment is portable and supports image triggers through annotations.

v.q: Which resource type should a new application use for a stateless service?
v.w: DeploymentConfig is deprecated. A standard Deployment works on any Kubernetes.
